exposure: progressive elevation of blood cell count
negative results of vaginal secretion re-examination
residual cervical length (10-20 mm, >=20 mm, <=10 mm)
outcome: delivery before 34 weeks of gestation (preterm birth)
cohort: The study included 348 second-trimester patients with cervical insufficiency.
finding: Screening and treatment of vaginal secretions, monitoring blood counts, and timely cervical cerclage significantly improve gestational age prolongation and reduce preterm birth before 34 weeks and severe neonatal complications in patients with cervical insufficiency.
gest_age: The study focused on factors influencing delivery before 34 weeks of gestation in second-trimester patients.
